title: Establish observability baseline for analytics ingestion & query services
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Provide a minimum production-grade observability surface for the Console analytics backend (ingestion, transformations, storage, query API) so SRE/infra and product teams can detect regressions, understand failures, and measure user-facing impact. This ticket establishes SLIs/SLOs, tracing spans and propagation conventions, structured log schema, and a set of dashboards and alerts for the initial rollout.

Scope of work:
- Define SLIs and SLO targets for ingestion and query paths.
- Add standardized tracing spans and ensure trace_id / request_id propagation across services (producer -> pipeline -> storage -> query).
- Normalize structured logs (JSON) with required fields for analytics events and control-plane traces.
- Build Grafana dashboards: ingestion lag, throughput, error breakdown, per-tenant p95/p99 query latency, and error budget burn.
- Create alert rules and PagerDuty playbook for SLO breaches and ingestion pipeline backpressure.
- Backfill missing metrics from historical data where possible and add telemetry gating for rollout.

Proposed SLIs & SLOs (initial):
- Ingestion success rate (events that reach storage / events received): SLO 99.95% monthly. Alert if 3h rolling <99.9%.
- Ingestion pipeline end-to-end latency (ingest receive -> persist): p95 < 5s, p99 < 30s.
- Query latency for Console analytics API (small payloads): p95 < 200ms, p99 < 800ms (production tier).
- Query availability (HTTP 2xx within 2s): SLO 99.9% monthly.
- Error budget policy: automated throttling fallback if query error budget burn >25% in 1h window.

Tracing & span conventions:
- Root trace starts at API gateway: span name api.console.analytics.request.
- Canonical span names: analytics.consumer.ingest, analytics.pipeline.transform, analytics.storage.write, analytics.query.handler, analytics.query.execute, analytics.cache.hit/miss.
- Required span tags/attributes: trace_id, request_id, tenant_id, route_id, model_id (if applicable), batch_size, payload_bytes, sample_rate.
- Propagation: use W3C traceparent for cross-service traces; add custom header X-Console-Req-Id populated on ingress.

Structured logging schema (JSON fields required):
- timestamp, level, service, span_id, trace_id, request_id, tenant_id, route, event_type, error_code (nullable), duration_ms (nullable), message, metadata (freeform string).
- Example event_type values: ingest.received, ingest.persisted, transform.failed, query.started, query.completed, query.failed.
- Ensure logs include at least one of trace_id|request_id for correlation with traces/metrics.

Metrics and tags:
- Counters: analytics.ingest.received, analytics.ingest.persisted, analytics.ingest.failed, analytics.query.requests_total, analytics.query.errors_total.
- Histograms: analytics.ingest.latency_seconds, analytics.query.latency_seconds.
- Labels/tags: tenant_id, region, instance_type, route, priority.

Dashboards & alerts:
- Ingestion Overview: throughput (events/sec), p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, backpressure/backoff counts, top error types by percent.
- Query Service Health: per-tenant p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, cache hit rate, active concurrent queries.
- SLO Burn Dashboard: current burn, 24h trend, owners and recent incidents.
- Alerts: SLO breach (pager), ingestion error spike (>1% error rate sustained 10m), ingestion lag >30s p99, query p95 > 400ms for 5m.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All spans listed are emitted in staging and production for sample requests and can be visualized in traces UI.
2) Structured logs conform to schema and can be filtered by tenant_id and request_id.
3) Metrics emit to the metrics backend with the listed names and tags; dashboards show expected graphs on staging.
4) SLOs defined in Grafana/Prometheus and basic alerting rules created with runbook links.
5) Deployment runbook & rollback steps documented; rollout gating in feature flags.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): Instrumentation + dashboards, 2-week soak. Owner: Rohit.
- Phase 2 (canary production): 10% traffic, monitor error budget and ingestion latency, revert flag ready.
- Phase 3 (full): 100% traffic and enable SLO-based alerts.

Backfill strategy:
- Backfill basic counters (ingest.received, persisted) for last 30 days from Kafka offsets and S3 logs into metrics backend. Backfill job tracked in ENG-4167.

Operational runbooks & playbooks:
- PagerDuty playbook for ingestion spikes and query latency degradation.
- Quick triage steps: check consumer lag, storage write errors, transformation error rates, and recent deploys.

Notes & trade-offs:
- We will keep sampling rate at 10% for full traces initially to control cost; increase for affected tenants during incidents.
- Avoid instrumenting every micro-surface synchronously: focus on the analytics critical path first, then expand.
- Logging verbosity gated by tenant-level config to control ingestion costs for high-volume customers.

Deliverables & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Analytics+Observability+Baseline
- Dashboards (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics-ingest-overview
- GitHub PR (instrumentation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2345
- Backfill job PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789
acceptance_criteria: Traces for ingestion and query paths visible in traces UI for sampled requests.
Structured logs emitted and parsable, with cross-correlation via trace_id/request_id.
Metrics exist for counters and histograms with specified tags; staging dashboards populated.
Grafana SLOs and alert rules created with runbook links and test alert firing in staging.
Rollout gating (feature flag) and rollback documented and tested in canary.
